title: Important Office Reminders and Procedures
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
NOTES 

FROM 

THE 

OFFICE NOTES FROM THE OFFICE

zoom_out_map Student Fees:Fees have been loaded to PaySchools if you wish to pay online. You can also pay in the office with cash or check.Lunch Accounts:As a reminder, you are able to add funds to your student's lunch account through the PaySchools system. If your student's account reaches -$50 it will be rolled into your school fees. Please be mindful and keep your student's account current. You can use PaySchools, send a check or cash to the school office to take care of your student's balance. The link for PaySchools is attached here; PaySchools Central.Free and Reduced:If you would like to apply for free or reduced lunches, please reach out to the Marshall office or the Marshall social worker Chrissy Rolfes at rolfesc@talawanda.org. We can help walk you through the online application or help you fill out a paper form in the office. If you qualify for FREE lunch, your fees will also be waived. (EXCEPT for 5th grade Chromebook fee) If you qualify for REDUCED, fees will be reduced by 85% (EXCEPT for 5th grade Chromebook fee) and meals will be FREE.Dismissal:Thank you for your help in keeping dismissal safe and smooth for everyone. We ask that when your child is called to your car, you please help them climb in and then pull forward to the upper lot to buckle them into their car seat. Remaining stopped in the dismissal lane to buckle your child slows down the process for all families and, more importantly, it creates an unsafe situation when other cars attempt to go around. Your cooperation makes dismissal safer and quicker for all of our students.Final Forms:Remember, if you have any changes to your information (phone number, address, who can pick up your student, etc) throughout the school year, change it in Final Forms! The office is notified of these changes and will update our information. IF you have an address change, you must submit new proof of residency to the office before we will update your address.

summary: **Student fees** are now available to pay online through [PaySchools Central](PaySchools) or in the office with cash/check. **Lunch accounts** should be kept current; balances reaching -$50 will be added to school fees. Families can apply for **free or reduced lunch** by contacting the Marshall office or social worker Chrissy Rolfes at rolfesc@talawanda.org (free lunch also waives most fees). For **dismissal safety**, please pull forward to the upper lot to buckle children after they enter your car. Update any contact or address changes through **Final Forms** (address changes require new proof of residency submitted to the office).

title: K-5 Grading System Changes for 2026-2027
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
DISTRICT 

INFORMATION DISTRICT INFORMATION

Changes to the K-5 Grading System at Talawanda NEW for the 2026-2027 School Year Grades 3-5 - Moving to a Traditional Letter Grading System (A-F)We are excited to shift our grades 3–5 to a traditional letter grade system (A-F) to provide a more detailed look at your child's overall performance and academic habits. This change aligns our 3rd-5th graders with the expectations they will meet in middle and high school, fostering greater accountability and preparing them for future success.For families, this transition offers a familiar and intuitive way to track progress. While the numerical scale focused on specific milestones, letter grades allow for a wider range of feedback to distinguish between meeting basic requirements and consistently exceeding them. This system ensures a clearer dialogue between teachers and parents, highlighting exactly where a student excels or may need extra support.Here is the breakdown of the traditional letter grading system:A - 90-100%B - 80-89%C - 70-79%D - 60-69%F - 0-59%Grades K-2 - Remaining with the Numerical Grading System (1-4)Grades K–2 will continue using the numerical (1–4) grading system to best support our youngest learners. At this foundational level, education is focused on the progressive development of core skills and meeting specific developmental milestones rather than a cumulative letter grade. The 1–4 scale provides a precise way for teachers to communicate exactly where a student is in their learning journey—from beginning to explore a concept to achieving mastery—ensuring that families have a clear understanding of their child's growth in these critical early years.As a reminder, here is a breakdown of the numerical scores:4 - Consistently/Independently Meeting the Standard3 - Meeting the Standard2 - Approaching the Standard1- Not Yet Meeting the Standard

summary:
**New grading systems effective for the 2026-2027 school year:**
- **Grades 3-5**: Transitioning to traditional **letter grades (A-F)** to align with middle/high school expectations and provide clearer feedback on performance (A: 90-100%, B: 80-89%, C: 70-79%, D: 60-69%, F: 0-59%)
- **Grades K-2**: Continuing with the **numerical system (1-4)** to track developmental milestones (4: Consistently/Independently Meeting Standard, 3: Meeting Standard, 2: Approaching Standard, 1: Not Yet Meeting Standard)

We are making math fact fluency a building-wide focus at Marshall! We challenge all Marshall families to spend 5–10 minutes each day practicing math facts together.

summary: Marshall is launching a building-wide **Math Fact Fluency Challenge** and encourages all families to spend **5–10 minutes each day** practicing math facts together. Math fact fluency means knowing addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division facts accurately, quickly, and flexibly. Families can help by playing card games, dice games, board games, or asking math questions during everyday activities like cooking, shopping, or driving.

title: Volunteer and Visitor Policy Requirements
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
VOLUNTEER 

& 

VISITOR 

POLICY VOLUNTEER & VISITOR POLICY

As we continue with our volunteer policy this year, please remember that any adult volunteer who wishes to enter the school building must have a volunteer application on file with the office every school year. After a parent’s second visit to the building, they are required to complete fingerprinting and a background check through the Central Registration Office. Please plan to complete this process at least 3 weeks prior to the event. This allows adequate time for the background check to be completed and for the appropriate information to be provided to the school administrator for planning purposes. Once completed, your background check is valid for 5 years.Central Registration Office:Ruth Michael📞 513-273-3101We appreciate your understanding and cooperation as we work to keep our students, staff, and school community safe. Public schools have implemented these regulations to comply with state and federal safety requirements regarding volunteers and visitors in schools.

summary: All adult volunteers must have a volunteer application on file each school year. After a second visit, volunteers must complete **fingerprinting and background check** through the Central Registration Office at least **3 weeks prior** to events. Background checks are valid for 5 years. Contact Ruth Michael at **513-273-3101** for Central Registration.

blocks.content: Health Education Curriculum Update - SB 288-Erin's Law The Ohio Department of Education and Workforce (DEW), formally called the Ohio Department of Education, has shared with public schools across the state Senate Bill 288. This legislation requires that health education curricula be updated to include (K-12/developmentally appropriate) prevention education information in the areas of sexual abuse and sexual violence for students in public schools.As promised, the district is providing an opportunity for families to review the curriculum, and parents may opt their students out of the lessons if they choose.  For more information from the Ohio Department of Education- Click HERE. Instruction occurs annually. This year the district will conduct these updates with students October 12-26, 2026.K-3 Curriculum- Click HERE4-6 Curriculum- Click HERE7-8 Curriculum- TMSSocial Inclusion: Click HEREDating Violence: Click HERESuicide Prevention: Click HERE9-12 Curriculum - THS will share their videos in three successive weeks. summary: Ohio Senate Bill 288 (Erin's Law) requires K-12 schools to include developmentally appropriate sexual abuse and violence prevention education in health curricula. **Talawanda will conduct these lessons October 12-26, 2026**, with annual instruction thereafter. Curriculum materials are available for parent review by grade level (K-3, 4-6, 7-8, 9-12) covering topics including social inclusion, dating violence, and suicide prevention. **Parents may opt their students out** of these lessons - contact your student's school counselor with questions.

It was wonderful seeing some of our Marshall families in the building for conferences this week! If you weren’t able to meet with your child’s teacher this week, we will be here Tuesday! Please reach out to your child’s teacher to sign up for a time. During Family Groups this week, we also had a great time cheering on our friends who participate in Marshall Running Club! We love celebrating and supporting one another! Just a reminder that there is no school on Friday, October 16th. We hope everyone has a wonderful weekend!Stephanie JonesPrincipal
